0.1 This Indian Standard (First Rcv ision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 January 1~7,j, after the draft finalized by the Pcst Control Sectional Cornmiucc had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first issued in 1966. I n this standard the requirements were based on the material which was being imported into the country. "Oith production of dirncthoatc, technical having' been commenced in the country, the technical committee responsible for the formulation of this specification decided to issue this revision. Accordingly, in this revision, req uircmcn ts for various charactcrist ics have been reviewed in the light of experience gained in the country. Requirements for active ingredient content and acidity have been modified, 0.3 Dirncthoatc, technical is used in the preparation of formulations used in the control of a broad range of insect pests and mites. Dirnethoate is primarily a systemic insecticide but also possesses properties of a contact insecticide and an acaricide. 0.3.1 Dimethoate is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO) for the pesticidal chemical 0, 0dimethyl S-( "'''.methylcarbamoyhncthyl) phosphorodi thioate as its active ingredient. The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of this product are given below:

Empirical Formula C.H1,NOaPS.

Structural Formula

Molecular Mass

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

DETERMINATION OF DIMETHOATE CONTENT A-O. GENERAL
A-O.l For the determination of dimethoate content, two methods have been prescribed. The Infrared Spectrophotometric method shall be referee method in case of dispute.

A-I. INFRARED SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC METHOD
A-I.I Principle - The sample is dissolved in carbon disulphide, Tlie absorbance of the extract is compared to that of the absorbance of an extract of a standard by infrared spectrophotometer. A.I.2 Apparatus

A-l.2.1 Infrared Sprciropl,olomtttr - capable of reading in the region of 9"1 to 11�2 micron, with the slit width, gain and response time and scaning speed adjustable to produce satisfactory signal-to-noise ratio and adequate resolution under the conditions of the test.

A.l.2.2 Absorption Cells - sealed cesium iodide absorption cells, having internal light path of about 0-1 mm,
A-l.2.3 H..l'Podermic Syring, 5 and 2-ml capacity.

A-l.3 Reageats
A-I.3.1 Dimethoate - standard of known purity. A.l.3.2 Carbon Disulphide analytical grades reagent.

A.l.4 Procedure

A-I.f.l Calibration
A-l.4.1.1 Weigh accurately a quantity of standard dimethoate to give a 10 mg per ml solution with carbon di-sulphide in a suitable volumetric flask.
A-l.4.1.2 Fill the absorption cell with carbon disulphide. Adjust the spectrophotometer for the optimum instrument setting with respect to gain, slit width, response, speed and drum drive. Make scan with carbon disulphidc in the cell over the wave length region 9"1 to 11�2 micron.

6

IS � 3902. 1975
A-l.f.l.3 Turn the wave length scale back to its original setting. Fill the cell with solution ( see A-I.f.I.1 )_ Make a scan in the wave length region of 9-1 to 11'2 microns, with the same setting as previously used ( se� A-I.4.1.2 ). A-I.4.1.4 With the base line drawn from 9-1 to 11�2 microns, measure the absorbance of the solution at 9�8 micron. A-J.4.2 Estimation of Active Ingredient in the Material Weigh accurately a quantity of sample to give a 10 mg per ml solution of active ingredient with carbon di-sulphide in a suitable volumetric flask.
�-:

A-l.4.2.1 Make a scan of carbon disuJphide and the carbon disulpl.idc solution of the material ( see A-l.4.2 ) as prescribed under A-J.4.J.2 and A-l.4.1.3 using the same cell and setting. Measure the absorbanccs as prescribed in A-l.4.1.4.

liquid partition chromatography using isopropyl ether petroleum ether mixture as moving phase and water as static phase on kieselguhr. 0,0, S-trimethylphosphorodithioate precedes dimethoatc; dimcthy lphosphorodithioic acid and other more hydrophilic impurities follow the 'active' peak. Therefore, several columns should be packed and checked before indulging in their use. The reproducibili ty should be determined in triplicate with at least three samples of dimethoate having different purities, The triplicate determination should agree within � 1 percent.

A-2.2 Apparatus A-2.2.1 Chromatographic Column - a glass tube of 1,,1 mm inside diameter

.A-2.3 ReageDts
A-2.3.1 l/yjio-Super.Cel -

A-2.3.2 Petroleum Ether - aromatic fr e e, boiling range from 60 0 to ao�c. Can be rendered aromatics free by shaking with concentrated sulphuric acid.
A-2.3.3 Mixed Solvent - prepared by mixing equal volumes of technical isopropyl ether and petroleum ether ( aromatic-free, boiling range from 60 to 80�C) and filtering through ether.. extracted cotton \\�001.

A-2.3.4 Diethyl Ether -- reagent grade.
A-2.3.5 Nitric Acid - sp gr 1'42. A-2.3.6 Perchloric Acid 60 percent,

A-2.3.7 Ammonium Molybdate Solution - prepared by dissolving 50 g of ammonium molybdate in one litre of water,

A-2.3.8 Ammonium Vanadate Solution - prepared by dissolving 2�5 g of ammonium vanadate 1: '19 ( v/v) nitric acid and made to one litre.
A-2.4 Procedure

A-2.4.t Preparation of Column - Weigh 20 g of Hyflo-Super-Cel and transfer the same to a mortar. Add dropwisc, constantly stirring, 10 ml of distilled water with the help of a pipette. Triturate gently but thoroughly to homogenize the mixture, Add sufficient quantity of the mixed solvent to form a thin slurry and mix well. Plug the bottom of the column with a small wad of ether extracted cotton \\'001. In order to help the cas)' rotation of the tube and at the same time to keep it firm in its vertical position under pressure, fix the tube with the help of t\VO clamps one placed just below the constriction of the tube and another near the top of the column. Pour the slurried Hyflo-Supcr-Ccl into the tube and pack the first 0�5 cn1 of the column relatively firmly in order to provide a sound base fur the column, Gently lower the packer disc from a position 3 to 4 em above the packed surface so as to compress 1 to 2 em of the material, Rotate the lube and with short strokes and applying minimum pressure, consolidate the edge of the column taking care that only a small amount of the slurry is pushed down and no air enters into the column 8

IS I 3902 � 1975
during operation. Repeat this process until the whole of the Hytlo-SuperCe.l has been packed in 1 to 2. mm sections and the. column is uniformly b~1l1t. ''''ash the column with 100 ml of the nuxed solvent applying nitrogen pressure.

A-2.4.2 Standardization of Column - Dissolve 1 g of dimethoate in 100 ml of ether. Transfer 1 011 of the solution to the column from a l-rnl graduated pipette. By, applying nitrogen pressure at the top of the column, force the solvent carefully through the column until its surface coincides with the .surface of the packing. Carefully release the pressure and wash the solution on to the column with t\VO I-ml portions of mixed solvent. Elu.te with ~ixed solvent at the rate of 2'5 to 3�0 ml per minute by application of nitrogen pressure to the top of the reservoir, collecting lO-ml fractions. Tra nsfcr the fractions quantitatively to, 50-rol Kjeldahl flasks, add 5 to 7 ml water and evaporate the organic layer on a steam-bath blowing off the last traces with a hand bulb. Determine the total phosphorus as described under A-2.4.3 from an average column) dimethoatc is eluted in fraction 10, 11 and 12. A-2.4.3 Analysis ofSample
A-2.4.3.1 Preparation of solution - Weigh O'S g of the technical material into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in diethyl ether and make up to the mark with diethyl ether. Mix well and continue as given

in A-2.4.3.2.
A-2.4.3.2 Chromatographic separation of dimethoat� - Pipette 1 ml of the diethyl ether solution on to the column and wash in with two l-rnl portions of mixed solvent as described under A-2.f.2. Great care shall be taken to avoid errors in pipetting 1 ml of solution. The temperature of the aliquot taken shall be the same as the temperature at which the 50 ml was measured. All possibilities of evaporation of solvent before and during pipetting shall be avoided, Elute with mixed solvent at the rate of 2'5 to 3-0 ml per minute collecting a 50 ml fraction as determined through standardization steps to contain all the dimethoate and separately 10 ml fractions from either side of the 50 mJ fraction. Transfer the 50 rnl fraction to a 250 ml conical flask, add 5 ml of water, and evaporate the solvent on a steam-bath. Blow off last traces of solvent with a hand bulb, Transfer the residue quantitatively to a 50 ml Kjeldahl flask, and 4 ml pcrchJoric acid and 1 ml nitric acid. Evaporate to fumes of perchloric acid and reflux gently for 3 to 5 minutes (set Note 1). Coo), add 10 ml water and boil gently for about 5 minutes. Cool, dilute with water to about 35 ml in a 50 ml volumetric flask, add 5 ml ammonium vanadate solution. swirl, add 5 ml ammonium molybdate solution, then dilute to the mark with water and shake.

IS I :4902 � 1975
Read the optical density against a reagent blank in a l-crn cell at 470 nrn after 30 to 40 minutes (Jet Note 2). Read, the equivalent phosphorus from a graph obtained using pure potassium dihydrogen phosphate. Transfer the 10 ml fractions directly to 50-ml Kjcldahl flask, add 5 ml of water, evaporate the solvent on a steam-bath, removing the last traces of solvent with a hand bulb. Proceed exactly as given in A-2.4.3.2 ( se� Note 3 ).

!':OTJ: 2 - The reagent blank shall be checked regularly against water. optical density should not exceed 0'010.

~OTE 3 - Neither of the fraction should contain phosphorus (if it docs, it should be within 0'002 of reagent blank). If phosphorus is found, the column should be' rr-st audard iz ed and, if necessary, discarded,
